premises: Dislocation pile-ups at semi-coherent phase boundaries in eutectic HEAs cause local stress concentrations and microcracking, limiting ductility.
Phase-selective recrystallization can fully recrystallize the soft FCC lamellae while preserving the hard B2/BCC phase and its boundaries.
Recrystallizing the soft phase reduces its internal dislocation density and diminishes dislocation accumulation at phase boundaries.
Preserving the hard phase and its strong semi-coherent interfaces maintains or enhances overall strength.
This treatment can significantly improve tensile ductility (e.g., ~35% uniform elongation) while retaining or increasing strength.
